lines.trans: Maksim, I carefully read your résumé.
I hope you liked my experience.
You are a very capable and promising cook.
Thank you, I truly want to learn a lot.
I will gladly take you into the kitchen.
At the Claude Monet restaurant they do not appreciate me.
I do not understand why they act like that.
There they only give me vegetables to peel.
With us you will cook complex dishes.
This is exactly what I dreamed about!
Here are my contacts just in case.
When should I expect your call?
I will call you in a couple of days.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.
How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?
Who are your rivals?
Is this your programme?
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: 'взять на работу' = to give someone a job
'взять на работу' = to give someone a job

examples.trans: Go and hire Galileo.
Take the money.

examples.text: Вот и возьмите на работу Галилея.
examples.trans: Then go and hire Galileo.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Read everything carefully!
Listen to the teacher attentively.

examples.text: И, Марина Сергеевна, читайте всё внимательно! Особенно мелким шрифтом!
examples.trans: And, Marina Sergeyevna, read everything carefully! Especially in fine print!
There, look.
Here's my toy car.
All right, here you go. There, look.

всякий.gloss: every kind of, all sorts of, any

meanings.en: all sorts of, every kind of
meanings.note: всякое бывает = all sorts of things happen
на всякий случай = just in case

examples.trans: Alright, all sorts of things happen.
Take an umbrella just in case.

examples.text: Ладно, всякое бывает. Ну что вы?
examples.trans: Alright, all sorts of things happen. Oh, come on.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.

examples.trans: I'm cooking lunch.
Mum cooks well.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!
Let's talk.
He gives me a book.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Настроение у меня действительно очень хорошее.
examples.trans: My mood really is very good.
This is indeed an important question.
Quiet, stop! It really hurts!

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: Good afternoon!
I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'call; bell' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'm waiting for a call.
Thanks for the call.

examples.text: Генерал Круглов ждёт звонка. Будьте любезны.
examples.trans: General Kruglov is waiting for a call. If you'd be so kind.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right

examples.trans: Exactly, quite right.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.
When?
When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.
Oh yeah? When?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'contact' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: All contacts go only through me.
Do you have his contact details?

examples.text: Будут разные провокации. Все контакты только через меня.
examples.trans: There will be various provocations. All contacts go only through me.
We're sitting in the kitchen.
Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.
I dream of the sea.
Dream on!
Dream on.

meanings.note: мы многое можем сделать = there is plenty we can do

examples.text: А мы многое что можем сделать.
examples.trans: Oh, there's plenty we can do.
Much has changed over this year.

examples.text: А мы многое что можем сделать. Вот, например, мальчик.
examples.trans: Oh, there's plenty we can do. Here, for example, is the boy.
Where's my toy car?
That's mine.
No. That's mine.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'деяться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hope, to rely on', paired with 'понадеяться'.

examples.trans: I hope you understood me.
I hope so. Go on, act quickly!
I hope so.

meanings.note: у + genitive = from someone: у меня научился

examples.trans: He learned that from me.

examples.text: А он с девочками разговаривать не научился.
examples.trans: And he never learned how to talk to girls.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.trans: I'm thinking about it.
We're talking about the town.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: plant or part of plant used as food

examples.trans: Fresh vegetables are very healthy.

examples.text: Там мне дают только чистить овощи.
examples.trans: There they only give me vegetables to peel.
Chop fresh vegetables for the salad.

meanings.note: + genitive or accusative: я не ожидал = I didn't expect (that)

examples.trans: I didn't expect that.
We are expecting guests.
Arkasha, I didn't expect that. Thank you!

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: They are building a centre.
History will punish them.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.
You will need my rich experience.
This life experience is very valuable.

examples.text: А вот тут вам понадобится мой опыт.
examples.trans: And right here you will need my experience.
I love our town very much.
It's very hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'pair, couple, match' in everyday Russian.

meanings.en: match (in a relationship: я не пара вам = I'm no match for you)

examples.text: Я понимаю, я не пара вам.
examples.trans: I understand I'm no match for you.
They are a very handsome couple.

examples.text: Я понимаю, я не пара вам. Вы красавец, а я старая.
examples.trans: I understand I'm no match for you. You're a handsome man, and I'm old.

examples.text: Ты молодой и очень перспективный руководитель.
examples.trans: You are a young and very promising leader.
The scientists developed a promising scientific project.

examples.text: Вы очень способный и перспективный повар.
examples.trans: You are a very capable and promising cook.
There is this English chef.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.
Call me this evening.
I'll call tomorrow.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: понимаешь? = you know? do you understand?

examples.trans: I understand.
I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.en: to be liked, to make a good impression
meanings.note: person who likes is in the dative

examples.text: Синеозерск понравился в Москве больше других мест.
examples.trans: In Moscow they liked Sineozersk more than other places.
Did you like the film?
Don't be afraid, you'll like it.

examples.text: Вика, так нельзя поступать со мной!
examples.trans: Vika, you cannot treat me like this!

examples.text: Я всегда стараюсь поступать честно, как он.
examples.trans: I always try to act honestly, like him.

examples.text: Я не понимаю, почему они так поступают.
examples.trans: I do not understand why they act like that.
Why are we going so slowly?
Why are you here?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'честь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to read (through)', paired with 'читать'.

examples.trans: First read the document.
He read the entire letter.
Here, read this and sign right here.

examples.text: Он бы сейчас до потолка прыгал от радости.
examples.trans: He would be jumping to the ceiling for joy right now.
What a joy to see you!

examples.text: Мы с радостью сообщаем вам новость. Ваш долг полностью аннулирован!
examples.trans: We gladly inform you of the news. Your debt is completely canceled!

meanings.note: document detailing qualifications and work experience

examples.trans: Max showed his résumé to the chef.

examples.text: Я принёс своё резюме для шеф-повара.
examples.trans: I brought my résumé for the head chef.

examples.text: Максим, я внимательно прочла ваше резюме.
examples.trans: Maksim, I carefully read your résumé.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ложный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('complicated, difficult').

examples.trans: Look, there's nothing complicated.
That's a very difficult question.
Danila, let's go. Look, there's nothing complicated.

meanings.note: на всякий случай = just in case

examples.trans: Take it, just in case.
This is a strange case.

examples.text: Возьмите, пожалуйста. На случай, если передумаете.
examples.trans: Please take this. In case you change your mind.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.trans: Thanks, Dad!
Thank you for your trust!

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пособный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('capable, able').

examples.trans: He is a very capable cook.

examples.text: Вы очень способный и перспективный повар.
examples.trans: You are a very capable and promising cook.

examples.text: Женщина не способна стать великим шефом.
examples.trans: A woman is not capable of becoming a great chef.

meanings.note: at the start of a question

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
That's good like that.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Everything's fine there.
Who's there?
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: 'а то' at the start of a sentence: 'а то мы уже начали беспокоиться' = we were starting to worry

examples.text: А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: We were starting to worry, you see.
Faster, or we'll be late.

examples.text: Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

examples.trans: I was only looking.
Just one.
I was only looking!
I have a toy car.
He's at our place.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.
I want coffee.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.en: to value, to appreciate, to esteem

examples.text: Город высоко ценит вас и вашего мужа.
examples.trans: The city values you and your husband highly.
I really appreciate your help.

examples.text: Слушай, Лёля, я очень ценю, что ты приехала.
examples.trans: Listen, Lyolya, I really appreciate that you came.

meanings.note: + accusative: через неделю = in a week

examples.trans: I'll come in an hour.
In a week.

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!
The cook peels bananas.
Better keep peeling bananas!

examples.text: Там мне дают только чистить овощи.
examples.trans: There they only give me vegetables to peel.
What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
